title: Pool chemical handling and storage at home
audience: Pool service technicians who handle, add or store pool chemicals at a home pool
learningOutcomes: Read the label and safety data sheet for a pool chemical before it is handled
Explain why chemicals are never mixed before they are added to the water, plus the risk involved
Pre-dissolve and add a chemical in the order and manner the label and the handbook describe
Store and separate chemicals so that children, incompatible products and the filter equipment are protected

instruction.heading: Why these products are hazardous
instruction.body: The UK handbook states that every pool chemical is potentially dangerous and needs careful handling. Each container carries the instructions for use and storage, and those instructions take precedence over habit or memory. Combining products before they reach the water can release a toxic gas or cause an explosion, and the handbook says this must never happen. The safety data sheet for each product lists its hazards, first aid, protective equipment and storage rules. Read it before handling the product and keep it where it is reachable reached on site.

instruction.heading: Adding a product safely
instruction.body: Dissolve each product on its own in a dedicated, labelled bucket filled with water drawn from the pool. Stir with a wooden or plastic paddle and pour the solution slowly near an inlet or around the edge of the pool, so it spreads without splashing. Undissolved product can mark the pool finish, so it must never be tipped in as a lump. Rinse the container in the pool once it has each use and avoid using it for a different product. Wash your hands afterwards, and keep children away from the chemicals throughout.

instruction.heading: Containers and storage
instruction.body: Never move a one chemical into the container meant for another product, and never reuse a used container from a different product. Keep the chemicals in a dry, cool, lockable place and separate each type from the others. The product manual for the filter asks for pool chemicals to be kept a stated distance from the filter, the pump together with the valve. Keep the store ventilated and away from fuel and heat.

instruction.heading: Empty containers and surplus product
instruction.body: The handbook directs that empty containers be rinsed in pool water and then discarded. Its household disposal route is UK practice and must not be used in Australia until the Australian disposal rules have been confirmed. Dispose of containers and surplus product by the route the label and the local authority require, and record which route you used. Never pour surplus product down a drain or onto the ground.

instruction.heading: What this lesson does not authorise
instruction.body: This lesson does not grant a licence, permit or authority to handle, store or transport dangerous goods, and it does not replace the operator's instruction or the product's safety data sheet. Treatment decisions are covered in “Disinfection chemistry and pH interpretation” and “Dosing systems and chlorine-gas prevention”.

procedure: Read the label and the safety data sheet for each product before handling it.
Put on the protective equipment the safety data sheet requires.
Check that the product is not being added to a container for another product.
Dissolve the chemical alone in a labelled bucket with pool water.
Add the solution slowly near an inlet or around the perimeter, without splashing.
Rinse the container in the pool, then wash your hands.
Return the product to its own labelled container and store it separately in the lockable area.
Rinse empty containers in pool water, and dispose of them and any surplus by the required route.
Record the product, the amount added, the time, the storage check and the disposal route.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks you to add two chemicals to the pool simultaneously to save time, and says you can mix them in the bucket first.
workedExamples.reasoning: Refuse to mix them. The handbook states that mixing chemicals before they are added can produce fatal gas or an explosion. Add each product separately, in its own bucket, and at a separate time, following the label. Record the refusal and the reason. Tell the customer why.

workedExamples.situation: You find a bottle of pool chemical stored beside a fuel can, with the cap loose and a child's toy on the floor next to it.
workedExamples.reasoning: Move the child away from the area and ask a responsible adult to take charge. Do not touch the spill or the loose bottle with bare hands. Move the fuel can and the chemical apart if it is safe to do so, using the product's safety data sheet. Record the storage problem, tell the owner, and refer it. Do not store the product back in the same place.

equipmentAndPpe: Safety data sheet for each product on site
Protective gloves, eye protection and any respiratory protection the safety data sheet requires
Dedicated labelled bucket for each product, with paddle
Lockable storage area and separate shelf or container for each product type
Waste container for empty product and rinse water

commonErrors.error: Mixing two products before putting them into the water
commonErrors.prevention: Add each product separately. Never mix them in the bucket or the container.

commonErrors.error: Using a container belonging to another product
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the original labelled container, and dispose of empties.

commonErrors.error: Adding undissolved chemical directly to the pool
commonErrors.prevention: Dissolve each product in its own bucket before adding it slowly.

commonErrors.error: Leaving chemicals within reach of children or near the filter equipment
commonErrors.prevention: Lock and separate the chemicals, and report any unsafe storage.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Never combine products before they are added to the water water. Mixing can produce fatal gas or an explosion.
Never decant one chemical into the container of another, and never use a used container from a different product.
Never let children handle pool chemicals.
Store chemicals in a dry, cool storage that can be locked, separated by type. Keep pool chemicals a set distance from the filter unit, pump, and valve.
Read the instructions for use on the container before any product is handled. Clean your hands after use.
Do not add undissolved chemical directly to the pool, because it can harm the pool finish.
This lesson grants no licence or permit.

qualityStandard: Each product is handled with its safety data sheet available and the required protective equipment worn.
No two products are mixed or combined before they are added to the water.
Storage is locked, separated and recorded as checked at each visit.
documentationEvidence: Record of product, amount, time and method for each addition
Storage check record, including separation and lock
Disposal record for empty containers and surplus product
summary: Pool chemicals are dangerous. Read the label and the safety data sheet first.
Never mix products. Dissolve each product alone and add it slowly.
Store chemicals locked, separated and well away from the filter and from children.

knowledgeChecks.question: Two chemicals are to be added to a pool. What is the correct practice?
options: Mix them in one bucket first and add the mixture to the pool
Add each product separately, dissolved alone in its own labelled bucket
Add both straight into the pool at the same spot
Store them together on the same shelf so they are ready to use

knowledgeChecks.question: A pool chemical is found next to a fuel can, and a child is nearby. What is the first action?
options: Add the chemical to the pool to clear the area and then stand the child by the gate
Leave it, because the child is not handling the product and nobody has touched the fuel can
Move the child away and ask a responsible adult to take charge, then deal with the storage
Pick up the spill with bare hands and store it at the back of the shed today

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the handbook say about an empty chemical container?
options: It should be left open near the filter until the next visit and the lid is left off to dry
It should be poured into the skimmer basket and the basket is then cleaned by hand at the pool edge
It may be used for another product if it is rinsed and then kept with the stock on the shelf
It should be rinsed in the pool's water and disposed of, and the disposal route must suit Australian rules
